doctrine: Only SYNTHETIC values may be allowlisted. A real person's NRIC is never allowlisted — the fixture must be replaced with a synthetic number instead. Every entry needs synthetic:true, a reason, and an approver; an entry missing any of the three is ignored and the value is scanned normally.
rule: This list exists so a control can be demonstrated without using the data the control protects. The audit that motivated the gate found a real third-party NRIC serving as the test fixture for a PII-redaction control in docs/blueprints/BEFORE-MODEL-CALLBACK-SPEC-v1.md — the control meant to stop leaks was proved with leaked data.

allow.reason: person_data_gate.py self-test fixture: structurally valid NRIC shape (date + place-of-birth code both pass validation) used to prove the positive arm fires.
self-test fixture: leap-day NRIC, proves the two-century date resolution accepts 29 Feb.
self-test fixture: NRIC adjacent to an age field, the shape in which real ones were found.
self-test fixture: documents that the gate is deliberately shape-based and will flag any structurally valid NRIC, including one used as an order id.
self-test fixture for the Telegram bot-token arm. bot_id 1234567890 is a reserved example id and the secret half is the literal word 'Synthetic'.

notes: The binary coincidences in the self-test (320193-20-0000, 193125-13-4165, 628280-16-0203, 140361-26-0353, 202601-15-1234) need no allowlist entry — they are rejected by date and place-of-birth validation before the allowlist is consulted.
Adding a real value here does not make the gate pass silently: entries without synthetic:true, reason, and approved_by are dropped by load_allowlist().
